identity.title: CAT-Q: Cost-efficient and Accurate Ternary Quantization for LLMs

problem.claim: Compress and accelerate large language models through ternary quantization.

gap.claim: Existing leading ternary quantization methods rely on costly, data-intensive quantization-aware training to address severe performance degradation.

contributions.claim: CAT-Q is a post-training ternary quantization scheme with learnable modulation and softened ternarization, coupled from an optimization perspective.
Learnable modulation adjusts weight distributions and ternary thresholds, while softened ternarization uses a differentiable transition to guide convergence.
The method is reported as applicable across diverse LLM architectures and model sizes, including models up to 235B parameters.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that CAT-Q is the first method to quantize much larger pre-trained LLMs of 14B–235B parameters into leading ternary models within 8–60 hours on eight A100-80GB GPUs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that 1.7B–8B-parameter pre-trained LLMs can be quantized using 512 calibration samples, with superior performance to BitNet 1.58-bit v1 and v2 models of 1.3B–7B parameters trained on 100B tokens.
The authors report an approximately 100,000× reduction in training tokens relative to those BitNet comparisons.
The authors report quantizing 14B–235B-parameter pre-trained LLMs into leading ternary models in 8–60 hours on eight A100-80GB GPUs.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper introduces ternary quantization for compressing and accelerating LLMs.
It positions CAT-Q as post-training quantization, avoiding the costly quantization-aware training used by existing methods.
CAT-Q combines learnable modulation with softened ternarization to reduce sensitivity and promote stable convergence.
The authors report strong results with 512 calibration samples for 1.7B–8B models and scaling to 14B–235B models within 8–60 hours.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links each component to a specific quantization difficulty: modulation addresses sensitivity, while softened ternarization addresses convergence.

lessons.interpretation: Mechanism-to-problem alignment makes a technical method easier to evaluate and understand.
lessons.application: When presenting a new method, map each component to the concrete failure mode it is intended to mitigate.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when component roles are not independently distinguishable or supported by evidence.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical accuracy metrics, datasets, evaluation tasks, or detailed definition of “superior performance” or “leading.”
The comparison may involve different training regimes and model families; the abstract does not provide enough detail to assess comparability.
The abstract does not specify calibration procedure, architecture coverage, or resource usage beyond the reported GPU count and time.
